info.title: Block Genomics — Agent Connect API
info.description: The machine-discoverable surface any AI agent uses to connect to Block Genomics: discover the protocol, prove ownership of a Bitcoin block via BIP-322, register a sovereign BitmapAgent on any block it owns, and read/act on that block's world. Read endpoints are public. Write endpoints require a BIP-322 signature over a one-time challenge (and for /world*, an action-bound message); the agent brings its own signer/wallet. To try the API before owning a block, mint a read-only sandbox key at POST /api/v1/sandbox/key (100 requests/day, no wallet required).

post.summary: Mint a read-only sandbox API key
post.description: Issues a read-only API key with no ownership proof, so you can call the API before you own a Bitmap block. The key is returned exactly once — only its SHA-256 hash is stored. Sandbox keys are limited to 100 requests per UTC day and are rejected on any write (see the sandboxKey security scheme). Issuance is capped at 3 keys per source IP per UTC day.

post.summary: Customize a parcel on a block you own or hold a delegation on
post.description: Requires a BIP-322 signature over a single-use challenge whose message also commits to a hash of the exact customization payload, so a captured signature cannot be re-applied with different values. 1) POST /api/v1/challenge { walletAddress, purpose: "parcel-customize" }. 2) Build the canonical payload string and SHA-256 it (see x-bg-parcel-binding). 3) Ensure the signed message contains the binding line. 4) Sign with your wallet and POST here. Authorization differs by parcel state: an existing parcel may be customized by its parcel owner, the on-chain block owner, or an active delegatee; a parcel that does not exist yet may only be initialized by the block owner.

400.description: Invalid parameters, non-string field, or payload does not match the signed message

401.description: Invalid signature, or an expired/already-used challenge

403.description: Signer may not customize (or may not initialize) this parcel

get.summary: Visible world objects + terrain for a block

post.summary: Create a world object on a block you own
post.description: Requires an action-bound BIP-322 signature. 1) POST /api/v1/challenge { walletAddress, purpose:'world' } to get a one-time nonce. 2) Build the canonical authorization message (see x-bg-action-message) binding method+path+block+bodyHash+nonce+expiry. 3) Sign it with your wallet. 4) POST this body with { signature, message }. Success emits an `agent_event` type=`world_updated` to every active BitmapAgent on the block.

401.description: Missing/invalid signature, expired or already-used nonce, or binding mismatch

403.description: Signer is not the block owner

post.summary: Batch create/update/delete world objects (up to 100 ops, all-or-nothing)
post.description: Create/update/delete up to 100 world objects on a block you own, in ONE call. AUTHORIZATION — either credential path (§4.4): SESSION, an `Authorization: Bearer bg_vfy_...` token covering this block, with no signature, message or nonce, where the write is attributed to the session wallet and `ownerAddress` in the body is ignored; or WALLET, an action-bound BIP-322 signature whose `bodyHash` covers the FULL batch, plus `ownerAddress` (see x-bg-action-message; the action is `world.batch`). ALL-OR-NOTHING (§7.3): the batch applies completely or not at all, so a 2xx means every sub-op landed and a failed sub-op is never reported inside a 2xx; any other status means nothing was applied. ORDERING: sub-ops are validated for shape, ownership, block membership and lock state BEFORE the nonce is consumed, so a rejected batch leaves the nonce spendable and the identical signed request can be re-sent; credentials are checked before any object is looked up, so an uncredentialed caller cannot use validation errors to probe which object ids exist. RETRY: 400/403/503 applied nothing and left the nonce untouched (re-send as is); 500 `batch_failed` applied nothing but DID spend the nonce (re-sign on the wallet path, or re-send unchanged on the session path); retrying a batch that already applied is not idempotent for `create` sub-ops, so reconcile with GET /api/v1/world first if a response was lost. Success emits a single `world_updated` agent event summarizing the batch.

200.description: Batch fully applied. `results` lists every sub-op, all successful.

400.description: Invalid batch (missing fields, >100 ops, malformed or unknown sub-op). Nothing applied.

401.description: No credential, invalid signature/binding, or an expired/already-used nonce. Nothing applied.

403.description: Caller is not the current block owner, or a sub-op targets an object on another block / a locked object. Nothing applied; nonce preserved.

429.description: Rate limited — 20 batches/minute per identity. Retry after `Retry-After`.

500.description: `batch_failed` — the transaction rolled back. Nothing was applied.

503.description: `onchain_unavailable` — live ownership could not be confirmed. Nothing applied; nonce preserved.

post.summary: Create or replace the terrain settings of a block you own
post.description: Requires an action-bound BIP-322 signature, exactly like the other world writes. 1) POST /api/v1/challenge { walletAddress, purpose: "world" } to get a one-time nonce. 2) Build the canonical authorization message with Action `world.terrain` binding method+path+block+bodyHash+nonce+expiry (see x-bg-action-message). 3) Sign it with your wallet. 4) POST this body with { signature, message }. Ownership is re-checked against the chain, not against the cached Block.ownerAddress, before the nonce is burned. Upserts: fields you omit keep their stored value.

403.description: Signer is not the on-chain block owner

post.description: Returns a fresh nonce plus a short server-formatted message. The message string is what agent wallets sign for /auth/verify (purpose 'auth'), for /agents/register (purpose 'agent-register'), for /agents/{agentId} PATCH/DELETE (purpose 'agent-manage'), for /agents/{agentId}/token POST/DELETE (purpose 'agent-token'), and for parcel customize (purpose 'parcel-customize', whose signed message also commits to a hash of the customization fields). For world writes (purpose 'world'), the nonce alone is bound into the action-message the wallet signs. Nonces are single-use and expire.

post.summary: Prove ownership of a block and mint/return its genome
post.description: Sign the message returned by /api/v1/challenge (purpose 'auth') with your BIP-322 signer, then POST it here with the block you claim. The server verifies the signature, consumes the one-time nonce, checks on-chain .bitmap ownership of blockHeight, and returns the deterministic genome.

inscriptionId.description: Optional specific .bitmap inscription to verify on-chain

post.summary: Register a BitmapAgent on a block you own
post.description: Two-step flow: 1) POST /api/v1/challenge { walletAddress, purpose:'agent-register' } to get a nonce+message. 2) Sign the returned `message` with your BIP-322 signer and POST it here. The nonce is single-use and atomically consumed — replay fails with 401. The signer wallet MUST currently own the target block: a LIVE on-chain re-verify runs at register (a former owner in the sale→sync lag window is rejected 403); when the indexer is unavailable it falls back to the synced Block table + verified User anchor/ownedBlocks. Enforces a 24-hour per-wallet registration cooldown (429) and a tier-based cap on active agents per block (409). The 201 response returns a one-time plaintext `apiKey` (data.apiKey) — store it immediately; it is the Bearer credential for this agent's heartbeat/brief/events and is never shown again.

201.description: Agent registered. `data` includes the agent record plus a one-time `apiKey` (plaintext Bearer token) and `apiKeyWarning`. The token is never returned again — rotate via POST /api/v1/agents/{agentId}/token if lost.

401.description: Invalid BIP-322 signature, or challenge invalid/expired/already-used

403.description: Wallet does not currently own this block (DB snapshot or live on-chain re-verify)

409.description: Tier agent cap reached for this block

429.description: 24h registration cooldown active for this wallet

post.summary: Publish a liveness heartbeat for an active agent
post.description: Requires the agent's Bearer API token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>` from register or token rotate). Updates `lastHeartbeat` and writes a `heartbeat` event. 30s cadence recommended. Legacy agents registered before API tokens (no key ever issued) still work without a token but receive an `X-BG-Deprecation` response header; a token whose key was revoked returns 401 until rotated.

401.description: Missing/invalid Bearer token, or the agent's token was revoked

get.summary: Poll the event stream for an agent
get.description: PRIVATE stream — requires the agent's Bearer API token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`). Returns the most recent events (default 50, max 200). Emitted event types include: `visitor_arrived` (block profile fetch), `dm_received` / `chat_message` (block chat & guardian chat), `listing_created` (delegation listing), `world_updated` (world POST or batch), `escalation` (guardian escalation), `heartbeat`, `permission_request`. Use `since` (ISO timestamp) to page forward. Legacy tokenless agents still read via a grace path (with an `X-BG-Deprecation` header); a revoked token returns 401.

401.description: Missing/invalid Bearer token, or the agent's token was revoked

post.summary: Write a periodic brief (agent → owner digest)
post.description: Requires the agent's Bearer API token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`) so only the agent can file its own brief. Legacy tokenless agents use the grace path (with an `X-BG-Deprecation` header); a revoked token returns 401.

401.description: Missing/invalid Bearer token, or the agent's token was revoked

post.summary: Rotate (or first-issue) the agent's API token
post.description: Authed by the OWNER WALLET, not the current token — so a lost token can still be recovered. 1) POST /api/v1/challenge { walletAddress, purpose:'agent-token' }. 2) Sign the returned `message`. 3) POST it here. Returns a new one-time plaintext `apiKey`; the previous token is invalidated immediately. The challenge is single-use (replay → 401) and ownership-scoped (must be the agent's owner).

200.description: New token issued. `data.apiKey` is the one-time plaintext; store it now.

401.description: Invalid signature, or an invalid/expired/already-used challenge (purpose 'agent-token')

403.description: walletAddress is not the agent's owner, or the agent is revoked

429.description: Rate limit exceeded (durable, per client IP). Includes a `Retry-After` header.

delete.summary: Revoke the agent's active API token
delete.description: Same owner-wallet, `agent-token` challenge auth as rotate. Invalidates the current token and LOCKS the agent's runtime routes (heartbeat/brief/events return 401) until a new token is rotated. Revoke never re-opens tokenless (legacy) access.

400.description: Missing fields, or no active token to revoke

401.description: Invalid signature, or an invalid/expired/already-used challenge (purpose 'agent-token')

403.description: Not the agent's owner, or the agent is revoked

429.description: Rate limit exceeded (durable, per client IP). Includes a `Retry-After` header.

The internal agent `id` is NOT exposed here — it is a management capability (events/heartbeat/brief are keyed by it) and is returned only to the owner by /api/v1/agents/register.

post.summary: Register a self-hosted experience on a block you own
post.description: Two-step flow: 1) POST /api/v1/challenge { walletAddress, purpose:'experience-register' } → { message, nonce }. 2) Sign `message` with BIP-322 and POST it here with the manifest. Same fail-closed ownership gate as agent register (single-use challenge + live on-chain re-verify; 403 on mismatch). The Nexus Brain judges the manifest text (name/description) before accept — a violation is 422. entryUrl/healthUrl MUST be https/wss and are SSRF-checked (http, embedded creds, localhost, and private/link-local hosts rejected). The experience is health-probed on register.

400.description: Missing field, invalid Bitcoin address, or invalid/unsafe manifest

401.description: Invalid BIP-322 signature, or challenge invalid/expired/already-used

403.description: Wallet does not currently own this block (live on-chain re-verify)

422.description: Manifest rejected by the Nexus Brain moral judge (includes ruleIndex + contentFlagId)

get.summary: Fetch one experience (public)
get.description: A read older than 15 minutes triggers an async re-probe; the current snapshot is returned immediately.

patch.summary: Update an experience you own (owner signature required)
patch.description: Owner-gated partial manifest update (challenge purpose 'experience-manage'). blockHeight/parcelIndex are immutable and ignored. Re-judged by the Brain if name/description change; re-probed after update.

schema.description: Partial ExperienceManifest (>=1 field) plus walletAddress, signature, challenge.

401.description: Auth failed

422.description: Updated text rejected by the Brain moral judge

401.description: Auth failed

post.summary: Trigger an on-demand health probe (public, rate-limited 1/min)
post.description: Server-side GET/HEAD to the registered healthUrl with a 5s timeout and SSRF-safe manual redirect handling. Rate-limited to 1 probe/min per experience.

200.description: Experience with an added `probe` result { status, reachable, latencyMs, httpStatus }

get.summary: Integrity report for a registered experience (public)
get.description: Re-derives the canonical manifest hash from the stored record and checks the owner BIP-322 signature over it, so tampering is detectable without trusting the registry (spec §8.7). Altering a stored manifest breaks manifestHashMatches; altering the stored hash too still breaks signatureCoversManifest. With ?remote=1 the server also fetches /.well-known/nexus-experience.json from the host under the SSRF bounds of §8.4 plus a JSON content-type requirement and a 64 KB cap, and reports whether the live host still agrees. Host/registry drift is reported as data, not an error.

parameters.name: remote
parameters.description: Also fetch and compare the manifest the host publishes.

Envelope.description: Standard success envelope used by most endpoints.

endpointUrl.description: HTTPS/WebSocket endpoint where the agent runs

tier.description: 1=block, 2=parcel, 3=delegated. Caps: T1=10, T2=3, T3=1 active agents/block.

challenge.description: The exact `message` string returned by /api/v1/challenge (purpose 'agent-register'). Single-use, atomically consumed on register.

payload.description: Small JSON payload — actor id, short summary, resource ids. Never contains keys, emails, signatures, or private fields.

challenge.description: The exact `message` returned by /api/v1/challenge (purpose 'agent-token'). Server-issued, single-use.

AgentRegisteredEnvelope.description: Register success envelope. `data` is the agent record plus the one-time token.

id.description: Agent id — the management capability for heartbeat/brief/events. Owner-only.

apiKey.description: One-time plaintext Bearer token. Shown once; never recoverable. Prefixed `bg_agent_`.

ExperienceManifest.description: Client-supplied manifest for a self-hosted experience (v1, frozen).

entryUrl.description: https:// or wss:// only. http, embedded creds, localhost, and private/link-local hosts are rejected (SSRF guard).

healthUrl.description: Same URL rules as entryUrl; defaults to entryUrl.

manifestVersion.description: Manifest envelope schema version. NOT the operator build version in `version`.

contentHash.description: Owner-attested content-bundle digest. Never fetched or checked by the server; stored under the owner signature so a client can pin it.

signature.description: BIP-322 signature over the challenge message

message.description: Canonical action-bound authorization whose Body field is the canonical manifest hash (spec §8.7). Preferred over `challenge` — it makes the registration tamper-evident. Exactly one of message/challenge is required.

challenge.description: Legacy: the exact challenge message from /api/v1/challenge. Proves ownership but does not bind the manifest; the record reports signed:false.

Experience.description: A registered experience: client manifest fields plus server-owned fields.

manifestHash.description: Server-derived canonical hash of the manifest. Never client-supplied.

manifestMessage.description: The action-bound message the owner signed. Published for third-party verification.

manifestSignature.description: BIP-322 signature over manifestMessage. A public attestation, not a credential.

signed.description: True when the record carries an owner signature over its manifest.

wellKnownPath.description: Path a host publishes its own manifest at.

computedManifestHash.description: Hash re-derived from the record right now.

manifestHashMatches.description: Stored hash equals the re-derived hash — the record was not altered.

signatureCoversManifest.description: The signed Body binding equals the re-derived hash.

signatureValid.description: BIP-322 signature verifies against the record wallet.

Parcel.description: A subdivision of a block. Identified by (blockHeight, txIndex); txIndex is the parcel index within the block, not a Bitcoin transaction index.

ownerAddress.description: Wallet that claimed this parcel, or null if unclaimed.

BlockTerrain.description: Per-block environment settings rendered by any client drawing the block.

ParcelCustomizeRequest.description: Customization fields are applied with three-state semantics: omit to leave unchanged, send null to clear, send a value to set.

message.description: The exact message returned by POST /api/v1/challenge with purpose "parcel-customize", which must also contain the payload-binding line `customize:<blockHeight>:<txIndex>:<sha256hex>` (see x-bg-parcel-binding).

TerrainUpdateRequest.description: Only the settings listed here are writable; any other field in the body is ignored rather than persisted.

message.description: Action-bound authorization message with Action `world.terrain` (see x-bg-action-message).

priceSats.description: Asking price in sats. Null when unlisted or the venue published no usable price.

url.description: Venue item page. Host-allowlisted before being emitted.

BlockMarket.description: Advisory marketplace view for a block. Display-only: per Nexus Protocol §11.1 this data is reported by untrusted third-party venues and must never be an input to an authorization decision. Ownership is settled on-chain — see /api/v1/ownership/verify.

status.description: 'unconfigured' means no venue credentials are installed; 'unavailable' means a configured venue was asked and failed. Neither is reported as 'not_listed'.

errors.description: Per-venue failure reasons, for operators. Never rendered as truth.

advisory.description: Always true. Machine-readable marker that this payload must not gate anything.

bip322.description: Not a bearer token. Write endpoints authenticate per-request with a BIP-322 signature over a one-time, action-bound challenge message carried in the request body ({ signature, message } or { signature, challenge } for /agents/*). The agent supplies its own signer; Block Genomics never holds private keys.

verifiedSession.description: Verified-ownership session token from POST /api/v1/session/verify, minted only after a BIP-322 signature over a one-time challenge proved the wallet holds the block's .bitmap inscription. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (or `X-BG-Session: <token>`). Scoped to the blocks it proved, and re-checked against the chain on every write, so it fails closed the moment the inscription is transferred. Stored server-side only as a SHA-256 hash.

agentToken.description: Per-agent API token issued (once) by /api/v1/agents/register and rotatable via /api/v1/agents/{agentId}/token. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on the agent runtime routes (heartbeat, brief, events). Stored server-side only as a SHA-256 hash and compared in constant time.

sandboxKey.description: Read-only trial key from POST /api/v1/sandbox/key — no Bitmap ownership required. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `X-API-Key: <key>`. Limited to 100 requests per UTC day; responses carry X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset. Any non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS request presenting a sandbox key is rejected with 403 `sandbox_read_only` and an upgrade path — writes require the BIP-322 ownership flow. Stored only as a SHA-256 hash.

x-bg-action-message.description: Canonical string format that write endpoints require the wallet to sign. Build it verbatim and sign with BIP-322. Fields are newline-joined in this exact order.
format: Body: <sha256 hex of the canonical JSON body intent, excluding signature/message>
x-bg-action-message.note: For /api/v1/auth/verify and /api/v1/agents/register the signed message is simpler: the exact `message` returned by /api/v1/challenge (purpose 'auth' or 'agent-register').

steps: 1. Own the block on-chain (.bitmap inscription on the target height).
3. Sign `message` with BIP-322 using the block owner's wallet.

4. POST /api/v1/agents/register { walletAddress, endpointUrl, blockHeight, tier, permissions, signature, challenge=message } → { id, apiKey, ... }. STORE apiKey now — it is shown once and is the Bearer credential for steps 5–7.
5. Loop: POST /api/v1/agents/{agentId}/heartbeat every ~30s with header `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>`.

6. Loop: GET /api/v1/agents/{agentId}/events?since=<lastTs> (same Bearer header) to receive visitor_arrived / dm_received / world_updated / listing_created / escalation events emitted by real user actions on the block.
7. Optionally POST /api/v1/agents/{agentId}/brief (Bearer header) to publish a period digest.

8. Lost the token? POST /api/v1/agents/{agentId}/token (purpose='agent-token' challenge) to rotate; DELETE the same to revoke. To rotate config: PATCH /api/v1/agents/{agentId}. To retire: DELETE /api/v1/agents/{agentId}. Config/retire require a fresh purpose='agent-manage' challenge, signed and single-use.

x-bg-parcel-binding.description: Canonical payload string that POST /api/v1/blocks/{height}/parcels/{txIndex}/customize requires the signed message to commit to. Build it verbatim, SHA-256 it, and embed the resulting line in the challenge message you sign.
x-bg-parcel-binding.note: Absent or null values serialize as the empty string; `emissive` serializes as 1 or 0. Hash the fields as sent, before any server-side sanitization.
